claims.say: Teams add a cache after observing a dependency's latency or efficiency at a request rate.
claims.quote: Many times this begins with an observation about a dependency's latency or efficiency at a given request rate.

claims.say: The most common expiry rule gives each object a TTL.
claims.quote: The most common policy uses an absolute time-based expiration (that is, it associates a time to live (TTL)

claims.say: On a cache miss a process recomputes the value.
claims.quote: To prevent multiple simultaneous recomputations of the same value, upon a cache miss a process will attempt to acquire the lock for that cache key and recompute it only if it acquires it.

claims.say: Under high request rate the database or other shared resource overloads.
claims.quote: When the request rate is high, the database (or any other shared resource) will suffer from an overload

claims.say: A cache stampede is a type of cascading failure in massively parallel systems.
claims.quote: A cache stampede is a type of cascading failure that can occur when massively parallel computing systems

claims.say: AWS calls it the thundering herd: many clients need the same uncached resource at about the same time.
claims.quote: the “thundering herd” situation, in which many clients make requests that need the same uncached downstream resource

claims.say: Stampede reduces the hit rate to zero and keeps the system in congestion collapse.
claims.quote: Thus, cache stampede reduces the cache hit rate to zero and keeps the system continuously in congestion collapse

claims.say: A lock: only the process that gets it recomputes; locking can prevent stampedes.
claims.quote: If implemented properly, locking can prevent stampedes altogether, but requires an extra write

claims.say: nginx cache lock: only one request at a time may populate a new cache element; others wait.
claims.quote: When enabled, only one request at a time will be allowed to populate a new cache element identified according to the proxy_cache_key directive by passing a request to a proxied server.

claims.say: The nginx cache lock is off by default.
claims.quote: Default: proxy_cache_lock off;

claims.say: Default lock wait is 5 seconds; then the request goes to the proxied server and the response is not cached.
claims.quote: Default: proxy_cache_lock_timeout 5s; Sets a timeout for proxy_cache_lock. When the time expires, the request will be passed to the proxied server, however, the response will not be cached.

claims.say: Others wait for a response to appear in the cache, up to the timeout.
claims.quote: Other requests of the same cache element will either wait for a response to appear in the cache or the cache lock for this element to be released, up to the time set by the proxy_cache_lock_timeout directive.

claims.say: A stale item can be kept and used while the new value is recomputed.
claims.quote: Keep a stale item in the cache to be used while the new value is recomputed

claims.say: nginx can use a stale cached response while it is updated, minimizing accesses to the proxied server.
claims.quote: Additionally, the updating parameter permits using a stale cached response if it is currently being updated. This allows minimizing the number of accesses to proxied servers when updating cached data.

claims.say: nginx can start a background subrequest to update an expired item while a stale response is returned.
claims.quote: Allows starting a background subrequest to update an expired cache item, while a stale cached response is returned to the client.

claims.say: AWS: weigh stale data versus errors.
claims.quote: evaluating when it is better for clients to see stale data versus errors.

claims.say: Probabilistic early expiration: each process may recompute before expiration by an independent probabilistic decision.
claims.quote: each process may recompute the cache value before its expiration by making an independent probabilistic decision

claims.say: delta is the time to recompute the value and scales the probability.
claims.quote: The variable delta represents the time to recompute the value and is used to scale the probability

claims.say: The authors show beta=1 works well in practice.
claims.quote: the authors show that setting beta=1 works well in practice.

claims.say: Early expiration takes more cache memory because delta is bundled with the item.
claims.quote: One drawback is that it takes more memory in cache as we need to bundle the value delta with the cache item

claims.say: The formula includes delta and the expiry time, so a longer recompute time makes early recompute more likely (derived from the formula).
claims.quote: if (!value || (time() - delta * beta * log(rand(0,1))) ≥ expiry)

claims.say: Locking requires an extra write (cost shown on recap).
claims.quote: If implemented properly, locking can prevent stampedes altogether, but requires an extra write

claims.say: AWS: choose when clients see stale data versus errors (cost of serving stale shown on recap).
claims.quote: evaluating when it is better for clients to see stale data versus errors.

claims.say: The lock default is off (share line on recap).
claims.quote: Default: proxy_cache_lock off;

claims.say: The stale-while-updating nginx parameter and background update are separate settings, default off.
claims.quote: Default: proxy_cache_use_stale off; Default: proxy_cache_background_update off;

share.who: the engineer who configures the cache in front of a busy backend or database
share.why: nginx's cache lock is off by default and its wait gives up after 5 seconds, so a cache can still send many identical requests to the backend

saves: the recap slide lists the defences (lock, stale copy, early refresh) with the cost of each
